# Per-user limits + cost

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P3 · Act as the user](../README.md#phase-3--act-as-the-user) · **Lane:** Worker · **Label:** `feature:per-user-limits` · **Epic:** [#150](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/150) · **Tickets:** 10 (4S 6M)

Operators can set rate limits and daily estimated-cost caps per verified user, optionally split by agent, so one user cannot use up a shared provider budget. Limits apply per request after an allow decision and never turn a deny into an allow. The control plane rolls up fleet spend per user per UTC day and publishes over-budget users on the signed policy wire, and the dashboard shows per-user requests, denies and estimated cost.

## How we build it

- Scope and gate: default off. With no `policy.userLimits`, `policy.defaultUserLimit` or `policy.anonymousLimit`, GET /policy and its ETag are byte-identical (golden test) and `BenchmarkEvaluate` shows no extra allocations. Limits are checked only after the existing allow decision, never turn Deny, NoMatch or Conditional into Allow, and never touch secret swap.
- Config (W-P3-PUL-01): new `config.UserLimit{Name, Match UserLimitMatch{Users, Groups, Agents, Domains []string}, PerAgent bool, RateLimit string, DailyCostUSD float64}`, `Policy.UserLimits []UserLimit`, `Policy.DefaultUserLimit *UserLimit` and `Policy.AnonymousLimit *UserLimit` (yaml/json omitempty). `Name` is required and unique in userLimits (agent-id charset); `default` and `anonymous` are reserved for the two single rules. Users and Groups use the W-P1-GPOL-01 normalizer; an email value matches only when `identity.Subject.EmailVerified`. Domains use the `policy.MatchDomain` dialect and empty means all domains. RateLimit uses the existing `validateRateLimit` (second, minute, hour). At most 256 rules. `config.LintUserLimits` warns on overlapping rules in one tier, dailyCostUSD with no CA, and agents whose identity mode is not require.
- Precedence: exactly one rule applies to a request. Tiers in order are rules matching by users, then by groups, then agents-only rules, then `defaultUserLimit`; within a tier the first rule in list order whose match fields and domains both match wins. A nil subject (no, invalid or expired token) uses only `anonymousLimit`, keyed by the worker's resolved agent id, and is never charged to a sub read from an unverified token. A strict per-user guarantee needs identity mode require; this is documented.
- Evaluator (W-P3-PUL-03): `EvaluateFor(domain, port, scheme, *identity.Subject) Result`, `PeekFor` and `identity.Subject` from P1 (W-P1-GPOL-02, W-P1-VRFY-01) are kept unchanged. New `ChargeUserLimit` and non-charging `PeekUserLimit` take the same arguments plus the agent id and return the P1 `Result` with two additive fields, `LimitRule` and `RetryAfter`. Bucket key `ul:<name>:<sub>` plus `:<agentID>` when PerAgent (anonymous: `ul:anonymous:anon:<agentID>`), so a rule has one budget across all its domains. Buckets live in a sharded map that `load()` does not re-make: `Replace` drops only buckets of rules whose canonical definition hash changed or that were removed, so blockedUsers or costBlockedUsers changes never reset windows. Expired buckets are swept about once a minute; at `maxUserLimitBuckets` (100000) a new key is denied fail-closed and counted.
- Proxy (W-P3-PUL-09): new `userLimitStage` in `runRequestStages` after identityStage, the W-P1-BLOCK-02 blockStage and the W-P1-GPOL-03 scopedPolicyStage, before judgeGate, charged per request so a keep-alive session carrying several users limits each correctly. h2 streams are charged in `serveGRPCStream`, WebSocket upgrades once per upgrade, and raw tunnels (no CA) once at CONNECT; a TLS-terminated CONNECT uses PeekUserLimit only. Over the rate: 429 `{"error":"user_rate_limited"}` with integer Retry-After. The worker heartbeat adds cap `userlimits/v1`.
- Cost input (W-P3-PUL-06): `recordAllowEvent` today prices from `req/resp.ContentLength` and clamps -1 to 0, so chunked and SSE LLM responses cost $0. Counting wrappers on the forwarded request body and the response copy (including relayMCPSSE and serveGRPCStream) supply the bytes actually relayed whenever Content-Length is unknown. This fix ships with no flag because it is a bug fix: streamed responses were priced at $0. Caps are on estimated spend (bytes/4 with the built-in prices in `cost.defaultProviders`) and are documented as such.
- Worker cost cap (W-P3-PUL-04): new `cost.Ledger` keyed by (UTC day, sub or anon key, rule name), owned by the worker and passed to the proxy, fed from `recordAllowEvent` and seeded at boot from the local SQLite store (sum of today's cost_usd by user_sub and limit_rule). Before a request to a destination `Estimator` tracks, the request is refused when spend so far is at or over the rule's DailyCostUSD, or when the wire lists the sub for that rule today: 403 `{"error":"user_cost_limited"}` with Retry-After to the next UTC midnight. When a cost-capped rule applies to a tracked destination that cannot be measured (raw tunnel, no CA, WebSocket), the request is denied with `user_cost_unmeasurable`. The cap is soft: it can overshoot by in-flight requests and by fleet sync lag.
- Analytics: reuse the P1 user columns, (user_sub, ts) index, `EventFilter.User`, ?user= filters and topUsers (W-P1-VRFY-03/04/06). W-P3-PUL-02 adds only `Event.AgentID` (json `agent_id,omitempty`) and `Event.LimitRule` (json `limit_rule,omitempty`) on the worker. W-P3-PUL-07 fills the existing fleet `agent_id` column at ingest (central_http.go stores only ProxyID today), adds `limit_rule`, and adds the rollup `user_usage_daily(day, sub, agent_id, limit_rule, email, requests, denies_json, cost_usd)` updated in the StoreAggregatedEvent transaction only when the event insert succeeded, so a retried batch never double counts. The rollup is kept 35 days regardless of events retention and maxEvents pruning.
- Fleet cost blocks (W-P3-PUL-08): the CP recomputes today's over-cap (sub, rule) pairs from the rollup on a 30s debounce after ingest and at startup, looking up each rule's DailyCostUSD by name in the served policy. It serves `costBlockedUsers: [{sub, rule, day}]` inside policyWire (sorted, omitempty, at most `config.MaxCostBlockedUsers` = 5000), computed state that is never stored in policy_versions so a rollback cannot clear it. Each change appends a `policy_publish_log` row with reason `user_cost` and calls Refresh, so W-P2-SBND-02 signed bundles get a new seq. One shared `config.ValidateCostBlockedUsers` runs on the CP and in parseRemotePolicy. Workers ignore entries whose day is not the current UTC day, so blocks lapse at midnight even when the CP is down.
- Degraded modes: CP down, workers keep the last-known-good list until each entry's day ends and their local ledger and rate buckets keep enforcing. Worker restart: ledger reseeded from local SQLite; rate buckets start empty (documented). IdP down: new tokens fail verification and fall into anonymousLimit. Rollup or recompute error: the CP keeps the last list and counts the error, never serving an empty list because of a failure. Analytics provider memory: the CP aggregator is disabled with one WARN.
- Dashboard (W-P3-PUL-05): `GET /dashboard/api/usage/users?window=24h|7d|30d&sort=cost|requests&limit=` (path chosen so it does not collide with the W-P3-OFFB-03 `/dashboard/api/users/{sub}/...` routes) returns per-user requests, denies by reason, estimated cost, top agents, matched rule, cap and today's block state from the rollup. It has a W-P1-SSO-05 authz row with role viewer and Scope `traffic:read` (W-P2-APIK-02). The Users usage view sorts by cost, flags users at or over their cap, drills down via ?user=, renders claims with textContent only, and warns when connected workers lack `userlimits/v1`.
- Observability: `RecordBlocked` for `user_rate_limited`, `user_cost_limited` and `user_cost_unmeasurable`, added to internal/proxy/reasons.go (W-P1-JAUD-06) and the warden.decision.v1 reason enum with a schema_rev bump (W-P1-JAUD-02). New OTel counter `warden.user_limit.denied.total{kind=rate|cost|unmeasurable}` and gauge `warden.user_limit.buckets`, never with sub, email or group labels. The decision log carries limit_rule. CP in-memory `warden_cp_cost_blocked_users` gauge and `warden_cp_cost_recompute_errors_total` counter are left for W-P5-RETN-06 to export.
- Rollout safety for cost caps: workers that enforce dailyCostUSD (W-P3-PUL-04) add `usercost/v1` to the heartbeat caps, because an older worker fails open on cost caps. A policy save that adds a rule with dailyCostUSD, or sets one on an existing rule, returns 409 `{"error":"workers_lack_capability","capability":"usercost/v1","workers":[ids]}` while any connected worker lacks that cap, unless the admin sends `force=true`, which is recorded in the admin audit row (the W-P2-WBND-07 pattern).

## Done when

On a managed deployment with two CA-enabled workers that advertise userlimits/v1, an operator sets `{name: eng-llm, match: {groups: [eng], domains: [api.openai.com]}, rateLimit: 60/minute, dailyCostUSD: 5}` and an anonymousLimit. A verified eng user over 60 requests a minute gets 429 user_rate_limited with Retry-After while another eng user on the same agent continues, and an unrelated policy or block-list change does not reset that window. A user whose streamed LLM calls push estimated spend past $5 gets 403 user_cost_limited on one worker, and within the debounce plus one long-poll cycle on the other worker through the signed costBlockedUsers entry; the block survives a worker or CP restart and lapses at the next UTC midnight even with the CP stopped. Dropping the token lands the request in the anonymous bucket. With no limits configured, /policy and its ETag are byte-identical. The Users usage view (viewer role or a traffic:read key) shows per-user requests, denies by reason, estimated cost and top agents, and no metric label carries a sub or email. A save that adds a dailyCostUSD rule returns 409 while a worker without usercost/v1 is connected, unless an admin forces it with an audited force=true, and the streamed-response cost fix (W-P3-PUL-06) ships without a flag.

### 1/10 · W-P3-PUL-01

**Add userLimits config, costBlockedUsers wire type and validation**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#151](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/151)

Add the per-user limit rules and the wire-only cost block list to config.Policy and to the CP policyWire, with one shared validator used by the YAML parse, parseRemotePolicy and the CP. Nothing enforces the rules yet, so a fail-closed guard rejects any non-empty userLimits, defaultUserLimit or anonymousLimit until W-P3-PUL-09 and W-P3-PUL-04 lift it, following the W-P1-GPOL-01 pattern. With none of the keys set, YAML, /policy and the ETag stay byte-identical.

**Requirements**

- New `config.UserLimit{Name string; Match UserLimitMatch; PerAgent bool; RateLimit string; DailyCostUSD float64}` and `UserLimitMatch{Users, Groups, Agents, Domains []string}`; `Policy.UserLimits` (yaml/json `userLimits,omitempty`), `Policy.DefaultUserLimit *UserLimit` (`defaultUserLimit,omitempty`) and `Policy.AnonymousLimit *UserLimit` (`anonymousLimit,omitempty`), added to rawConfig.Policy so strict YAML (KnownFields) accepts them.
- New `config.CostBlockedUser{Sub, Rule, Day string}` (json `sub`, `rule`, `day` as YYYY-MM-DD) and `Policy.CostBlockedUsers` (json `costBlockedUsers,omitempty`, yaml `-`, never accepted from local YAML). New `config.MaxCostBlockedUsers = 5000`.
- New `config.ValidateUserLimits`: Name required, unique and in the agent-id charset, with `default` and `anonymous` reserved for the single rules; each rule needs RateLimit and/or DailyCostUSD; RateLimit goes through the existing `validateRateLimit`; DailyCostUSD is 0 (no cap) or > 0 and <= 1e6; at most 256 rules; Users and Groups use the W-P1-GPOL-01 normalizer; Domains use the allowlist domain dialect. defaultUserLimit and anonymousLimit take no Match. Errors name `policy.userLimits[i].<field>`.
- New `config.ValidateCostBlockedUsers`: at most MaxCostBlockedUsers entries, sub non-empty and <= 255 bytes with no control characters, rule in the name charset, day a valid date; called from parseRemotePolicy so a bad row is rejected and the worker keeps its last good policy. Errors name the index, never the sub.
- Guard: validation rejects non-empty userLimits, defaultUserLimit or anonymousLimit with `not yet enforced`; W-P3-PUL-09 lifts it for rateLimit-only rules and W-P3-PUL-04 for dailyCostUSD.
- `Policy.DeepCopy` deep-copies UserLimits, every Match slice, both pointers and CostBlockedUsers. `controlplane.policyWire` gains UserLimits, DefaultUserLimit, AnonymousLimit and CostBlockedUsers (all omitempty), and `policyYAML` keeps the three YAML keys so `Server.WritePolicy` never drops them.
- New `config.LintUserLimits(cfg) []string` warns on overlapping rules in one tier, dailyCostUSD set with no CA configured, and agents whose identity mode is not require. Warnings carry rule names only.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/config/config.go: add UserLimit, UserLimitMatch, CostBlockedUser, the four Policy fields and the rawConfig.Policy keys.
2. internal/config/config.go: add ValidateUserLimits (reusing validateRateLimit and the GPOL-01 principal normalizer), ValidateCostBlockedUsers and the not-yet-enforced guard; call them from validate().
3. internal/config/remote.go parseRemotePolicy: run ValidateCostBlockedUsers and ValidateUserLimits on the decoded wire policy.
4. internal/config/config.go Policy.DeepCopy: copy the new slices and pointers.
5. internal/config: add new LintUserLimits and log its warnings once at worker startup and on CP policy load.
6. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: add the fields to policyWire and policyYAML and fill them where the policy server builds the wire.
7. Tests: validation table with indexes, DeepCopy aliasing, parseRemotePolicy round trip with the guard bypassed by a test hook, golden /policy body and ETag without the fields.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A rule with rateLimit `10/fortnight` fails with an error containing `policy.userLimits[0].rateLimit`: `go test ./internal/config -run TestValidateUserLimits`.
- [ ] A rule with neither rateLimit nor dailyCostUSD, a duplicate name, or the name `default` in userLimits fails and names the index.
- [ ] A wire policy with 5001 costBlockedUsers entries or an entry with day `2026-13-01` fails parseRemotePolicy and the worker keeps its last good policy: `go test ./internal/config -run TestValidateCostBlockedUsers`.
- [ ] Mutating `DeepCopy().UserLimits[0].Match.Groups[0]` leaves the original unchanged: `go test ./internal/config -run TestDeepCopy_UserLimitsNotAliased`.
- [ ] With none of the keys set, the /policy body and ETag equal the pre-change golden: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyWire_UserLimitsAbsentUnchanged`.
- [ ] Until the guard is lifted, a config with a non-empty userLimits fails to load with `not yet enforced`.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-GPOL-01`](identity-policy.md#19--w-p1-gpol-01) Add groups/users to allow entries and MCP conditions schema; [`W-P1-BLOCK-01`](user-block-list.md#19--w-p1-block-01) Carry blockedUsers in config.Policy and the policy wire

### 2/10 · W-P3-PUL-02

**Record agent id and limit rule on worker events**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#152](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/152)

The user columns, the (user_sub, ts) index and the Query Builder exposure already ship in W-P1-VRFY-03/04/06, so this ticket adds only the two fields per-user limits still need on worker events: the agent that made the request and the limit rule that applied. Both are omitempty, so events without them, receipts and sync payloads stay byte-identical. The fleet side is W-P3-PUL-07.

**Requirements**

- Do not redo user_sub, user_email, the (user_sub, ts) index, ingest pass-through or Query Builder work; W-P1-VRFY-03, VRFY-04 and VRFY-06 deliver them.
- `analytics.Event` gains `AgentID` (json `agent_id,omitempty`) and `LimitRule` (json `limit_rule,omitempty`). Existing field names and tags are unchanged.
- The single `p.recordEvent` from W-P1-VRFY-03 stamps AgentID from `identity.Subject.AgentID`, falling back to `proxy.Config.AgentID` (the id resolved by W-P2-AREG-05). LimitRule is set by W-P3-PUL-09 and W-P3-PUL-04; it stays empty here.
- Local SQLiteStore adds `agent_id` and `limit_rule` (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '') through addColumnIfAbsent and carries them in insertColumns, StoreEvent, StoreEventsBatch, the GetEvents scan and the GetOldestEventIDs scan so they reach SyncWorker. An index on (user_sub, limit_rule, ts) supports ledger seeding.
- `auditlog.FromEvent` maps both fields as optional properties of warden.decision.v1 with a schema_rev bump, so the W-P1-JAUD-02 leak-guard and reflection tests pass.
- Old DBs open with no data loss and a second open is a no-op.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/analytics/analytics.go: add Event.AgentID and Event.LimitRule.
2. internal/analytics SQLiteStore migrate: add the two columns and the (user_sub, limit_rule, ts) index via addColumnIfAbsent; extend insertColumns, StoreEvent, StoreEventsBatch, GetEvents and GetOldestEventIDs.
3. internal/proxy recordEvent (W-P1-VRFY-03): stamp AgentID from the request subject or p.cfg.AgentID.
4. internal/auditlog FromEvent and docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json: add `agent_id` and `limit_rule` as optional properties and bump schema_rev.
5. Tests: migration from a fixture DB, golden marshal of an Event without the fields, a recorded event carrying AgentID through the local store and the sync read.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A worker DB created before the change opens, gains both columns, keeps every row, and opens again unchanged: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestMigrate_AgentIDLimitRule`.
- [ ] An Event with no AgentID and no LimitRule marshals to the same JSON as before, so existing receipts verify: `go test ./internal/analytics ./internal/proxy`.
- [ ] A proxy event for a subject with AgentID `claude-code` is stored with agent_id `claude-code` and returned by GetOldestEventIDs.
- [ ] The W-P1-JAUD-02 schema tests pass with the new fields: `go test ./internal/auditlog`.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-VRFY-03`](identity-verification.md#37--w-p1-vrfy-03) Record user fields on worker events, receipts, decision logs and sync; [`W-P1-JAUD-02`](audit-log-export.md#46--w-p1-jaud-02) Publish decision v1 JSON Schema with closed-field and leak tests

### 3/10 · W-P3-PUL-03

**Add per-user limit matching and counters to the policy evaluator**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#153](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/153)

Teach internal/policy to pick the one user limit that applies to a request and to charge its rate bucket, without changing the P1 `EvaluateFor(domain, port, scheme, *identity.Subject) Result`, `PeekFor` or `identity.Subject`. User-limit buckets must survive `Replace`, because today load() re-makes the counters map and every costBlockedUsers or blockedUsers change would reset every user's window fleet-wide. This ticket is policy-package only; the PUL-01 guard still rejects userLimits, so merging changes nothing.

**Requirements**

- Keep EvaluateFor, PeekFor, Evaluate and identity.Subject unchanged. Add `ChargeUserLimit(domain string, port int, scheme Scheme, subj *identity.Subject, agentID string) Result` and non-charging `PeekUserLimit` with the same arguments. Result gains additive fields `LimitRule string` and `RetryAfter time.Duration`; over the limit it returns Decision Deny with Reason `user_rate_limited`.
- Selection: users tier, then groups tier, then agents-only tier, then defaultUserLimit; within a tier the first rule in list order whose match fields and Domains both match. Users match by sub, or by email only when EmailVerified. A nil subject uses only anonymousLimit. No matching rule means Allow with empty LimitRule.
- Bucket key `ul:<name>:<sub>` plus `:<agentID>` when PerAgent; nil subject `ul:anonymous:anon:<agentID>`. One budget per rule across all its domains.
- Buckets live in a new 64-shard map separate from e.mu that load() does not re-make. On Replace, buckets are kept for rules whose canonical definition hash is unchanged and dropped for rules that changed or were removed. Allowlist per-entry counters keep today's behaviour.
- Expired buckets are swept about once a minute, amortized on charge. At `maxUserLimitBuckets` (100000) after a sweep, a new key is denied with user_rate_limited (fail closed) and counted.
- New `MatchUserLimit(subj, agentID, domain) (UserLimitRule{Name, DailyCostUSD, PerAgent}, bool)` and `IsCostBlocked(sub, rule string, now time.Time) bool`, which builds its set in load() from Policy.CostBlockedUsers and ignores entries whose day is not now's UTC day.
- Hot path: with no user limits, BenchmarkEvaluate adds 0 allocations and changes by 5% or less; ChargeUserLimit with 256 rules stays under 1 microsecond per op.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/policy/policy.go load(): precompile Policy.UserLimits, DefaultUserLimit and AnonymousLimit into new []compiledUserLimit{name, tier, users, groups, agents sets, domains, parsedRateLimit, dailyCostUSD, perAgent, defHash}.
2. internal/policy/userlimit.go (new): sharded bucket map, ChargeUserLimit, PeekUserLimit, MatchUserLimit, the amortized sweep and the bucket cap.
3. internal/policy/policy.go Replace/load: keep the user bucket map, and drop buckets whose rule name is gone or whose defHash changed.
4. internal/policy/userlimit.go: build the cost-blocked set in load() and add IsCostBlocked.
5. internal/policy/policy.go Result: add LimitRule and RetryAfter fields.
6. Tests in internal/policy/userlimit_test.go: precedence, per-agent split, anonymous key, Replace preservation, sweep with a fake clock, cap, -race concurrency, and a benchmark.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With `{name: eng, match: {groups: [eng]}, rateLimit: 2/minute}`, alice's third charge is Deny/user_rate_limited while bob (eng, same agent) is still allowed: `go test ./internal/policy -run TestChargeUserLimit`.
- [ ] With a groups:[eng] rule and a users:[alice@corp.example] rule, verified alice is charged on the users rule, carol (eng) on the groups rule and dave (no group) on defaultUserLimit; an unverified alice email does not match the users rule.
- [ ] A Replace that changes only blockedUsers or costBlockedUsers keeps alice denied; changing her rule's rateLimit resets her bucket: `go test ./internal/policy -run TestReplace_KeepsUserBuckets`.
- [ ] IsCostBlocked is true for an entry dated today and false for one dated yesterday under a fake clock.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/policy -run TestUserLimit_Concurrent` passes.

### 4/10 · W-P3-PUL-04

**Cap daily estimated cost per user in the worker**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#154](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/154)

Add a worker-owned per-user, per-rule, per-UTC-day spend ledger fed from recordAllowEvent and seeded from local analytics at boot, and refuse requests to cost-tracked destinations once a user's spend reaches the rule's dailyCostUSD or the CP lists them in costBlockedUsers. Sessions that cannot be measured are denied for cost-capped rules instead of passing unmetered. This ticket is worker-only and lifts the PUL-01 guard for dailyCostUSD.

**Requirements**

- New `cost.Ledger` in internal/cost keyed by (UTC day, sub or anon key, rule name), bounded at 100000 keys, dropping previous-day keys at UTC rollover; owned by the worker and passed to the proxy through a new `proxy.Config.UserCost` seam, not stored in the evaluator.
- New `cost.Estimator.Tracks(domain) (provider string, ok bool)`. Only tracked destinations are subject to cost caps; untracked destinations are never denied for cost.
- At boot the worker seeds the ledger from the local SQLite store with a new `SQLiteStore.CostByUserSince(ctx, since)` (sum of cost_usd grouped by user_sub and limit_rule since UTC midnight, using the W-P3-PUL-02 index).
- In userLimitStage, before forwarding to a tracked destination with a matched rule that has DailyCostUSD: deny when ledger spend is at or over the cap, or when `IsCostBlocked(sub, rule, now)` is true. Response 403 `{"error":"user_cost_limited"}` with Retry-After in seconds to the next UTC midnight; the deny event carries Reason, the VRFY user fields and LimitRule.
- When such a rule applies to a tracked destination that cannot be measured (raw tunnel without CA at CONNECT, WebSocket), deny with 403 `{"error":"user_cost_unmeasurable"}`.
- recordAllowEvent adds the estimate to the ledger and sets Event.LimitRule. Add `user_cost_limited` and `user_cost_unmeasurable` to internal/proxy/reasons.go and the decision schema enum with a schema_rev bump, and call RecordBlocked; increment `warden.user_limit.denied.total{kind=cost|unmeasurable}`.
- The cap is soft: overshoot is bounded by in-flight requests on this worker plus fleet sync lag; documented in W-P3-PUL-10. Logs never carry email or per-user spend above debug.
- RemoteProvider.Heartbeat adds `usercost/v1` to caps once this ticket lifts the guard, so the CP can refuse cost-cap rules while older workers that would fail open are connected (W-P3-PUL-08).

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/cost/ledger.go (new): Ledger with Add, Spent and Seed; internal/cost/cost.go: add Estimator.Tracks.
2. internal/analytics SQLiteStore: add new CostByUserSince.
3. internal/worker/worker.go: build the Ledger next to cost.NewEstimator, seed it from the local store, and pass it in proxy.Config.UserCost.
4. internal/proxy/http.go userLimitStage (from W-P3-PUL-09): add the cost check using MatchUserLimit, Ledger.Spent and IsCostBlocked; add the unmeasurable check at CONNECT for raw tunnels and in ws.go.
5. internal/proxy/http.go recordAllowEvent: add the estimate to the ledger and set LimitRule.
6. internal/proxy/reasons.go and docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json: add the two reasons; internal/config: lift the guard for dailyCostUSD.
7. Tests in internal/proxy and internal/cost covering the acceptance cases with a fake clock.
8. internal/config RemoteProvider heartbeat: add the `usercost/v1` cap next to `userlimits/v1`.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With dailyCostUSD 0.01 and api.openai.com requests estimated at $0.006, alice's third request gets 403 user_cost_limited with Retry-After while bob is allowed and alice can still reach an untracked allowed domain: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestUserCostCap`.
- [ ] A wire entry `{sub: alice, rule: eng-llm, day: <today>}` denies alice on a tracked domain with no local spend; the same entry dated yesterday is ignored.
- [ ] After a simulated restart, the ledger seeded from the local store still denies alice: `go test ./internal/worker -run TestLedgerSeedFromStore`.
- [ ] With a fake clock past 00:00 UTC, alice's next tracked request is allowed.
- [ ] A raw tunnel (no CA) to api.openai.com for a subject with a cost-capped rule is denied at CONNECT with user_cost_unmeasurable.
- [ ] No user limits configured: existing proxy tests pass unchanged: `go test ./internal/proxy ./internal/cost`.

### 5/10 · W-P3-PUL-05

**Add per-user usage and cost dashboard view**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#155](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/155)

Give operators one place to see who is using which providers and how much they are spending. Serve per-user usage from the W-P3-PUL-07 rollup at a new route classified in the authz table, and add a Users usage view that flags users at or over their cap and warns when connected workers do not enforce user limits. The route path avoids the W-P3-OFFB-03 `/dashboard/api/users/{sub}` routes.

**Requirements**

- `GET /dashboard/api/usage/users?window=24h|7d|30d&sort=cost|requests&limit=` (default 7d, cost, 100; limit 1-500). Any other window or sort gives 400 `{"error":"invalid_window"}` or `invalid_sort`.
- 200 body: `{window, from, to, users:[{sub, email, requests, denies:{reason:n}, costUSD, todayCostUSD, topAgents:[{agentID, requests, costUSD}], limitRule, capUSD, atLimit, costBlocked}], unattributed:{requests, costUSD}}`. atLimit is todayCostUSD >= capUSD; costBlocked comes from the served costBlockedUsers.

- Fleet view: when the served policy has user limits, show 'N connected workers do not enforce user limits' for workers whose heartbeat caps lack `userlimits/v1` (W-P1-BLOCK-04, W-P1-GPOL-07 caps registry).

2. internal/dashboard/dashboard.go: register the route in dashboard.Routes() and add handleUserUsage with window, sort and limit validation and the shared cache.
3. internal/controlplane/authz.go: add the viewer / traffic:read row.
4. internal/dashboard/index.html: add the Users usage view, drill-down link and the fleet userlimits/v1 warning.
5. Tests: handler totals against a seeded fixture, 400 cases, atLimit and costBlocked flags, authz coverage, and an escaping test for an email containing `<script>`.

### 6/10 · W-P3-PUL-06

**Count relayed bytes for cost estimates on streamed responses**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#290](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/290)

recordAllowEvent prices requests from `req.ContentLength` and `resp.ContentLength` and clamps -1 to 0, so chunked uploads and chunked or SSE LLM responses, the normal shape for LLM APIs, are recorded at $0 and a daily cost cap would never fire. Wrap the forwarded request body and the response copy in byte counters and use the counts whenever Content-Length is unknown. Worker only; no new config and no flag, because this is a bug fix that ships on its own.

**Requirements**

- New `countingReadCloser` and `countingWriter` in internal/proxy record bytes actually relayed; they add no allocation per request beyond the wrapper.
- Wrap the request body after the secret swap and the response write path in the HTTP/1.1 relay, the relayMCPSSE stream path and serveGRPCStream.
- recordAllowEvent passes the counted bytes to `p.cfg.Cost.Estimate` whenever ContentLength is negative; fixed-length messages keep today's values.
- serveGRPCStream allow events gain CostUSD and Provider for tracked destinations, which they lack today.
- The changelog notes that cost_usd for streamed responses is no longer 0. No body content is logged or stored; only counts.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/proxy/counting.go (new): countingReadCloser and countingWriter.
2. internal/proxy/http.go: wrap s.req.Body and the response write in the relay and record the counts on requestScope.
3. internal/proxy/http.go relayMCPSSE and internal/proxy/grpc.go serveGRPCStream: use the same wrappers.
4. internal/proxy/http.go recordAllowEvent: use the counted bytes when ContentLength < 0.
5. Tests: chunked and SSE responses to api.anthropic.com record CostUSD > 0; a fixed-length response gives the same value as today; an alloc benchmark.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A chunked 40000-byte response from api.openai.com records cost_usd > 0: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestCost_ChunkedResponseCounted`.
- [ ] An SSE response through relayMCPSSE records cost_usd > 0.
- [ ] A response with Content-Length 40000 records the same cost_usd as before the change.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/proxy -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkHTTP -benchmem` shows no extra allocs per request compared with main.

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-PUL-04`](per-user-limits.md#410--w-p3-pul-04) Cap daily estimated cost per user in the worker

### 7/10 · W-P3-PUL-07

**Fill fleet agent_id and add the per-user daily usage rollup**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#291](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/291)

Control-plane half of recording. Ingest stores only ProxyID today, so the existing fleet agent_id column is always empty; fill it from Event.AgentID and add the limit_rule column. Add a per-day per-user rollup updated in the same transaction as the event insert, so fleet cost totals and the dashboard survive events pruning and are never double counted when a worker retries a batch.

**Requirements**

- `IngestHandler.ServeHTTP` (central_http.go) builds `AggregatedEvent{Event: e, ProxyID: proxyID, AgentID: e.AgentID}`; CentralStore keeps the field.
- FleetSQLiteStore adds `limit_rule` through the W-P1-VRFY-06 addColumnIfAbsent helper and carries it in StoreAggregatedEvent, GetEvents and GetAggregatedEvents.
- New table `user_usage_daily(day TEXT, sub TEXT, agent_id TEXT, limit_rule TEXT, email TEXT, requests INTEGER, denies_json TEXT, cost_usd REAL, PRIMARY KEY(day, sub, agent_id, limit_rule))`, upserted in the StoreAggregatedEvent transaction only when the event insert changed a row (event_uid dedup), for events with a non-empty user_sub or with a limit_rule of `anonymous`.
- The rollup is pruned to 35 days by its own step in prune(), independent of retentionDays and maxEvents.
- New `UsageByUser(ctx, from, to time.Time, limit int) ([]UserUsage, error)` and `TodayCostByRule(ctx, day string) ([]UserRuleCost, error)` on FleetSQLiteStore (parameterized SQL over the rollup) and on CentralStore (in Go), behind an interface so a later Postgres store can implement it.
- Old fleet DBs upgrade in place; events from old workers without the fields store empty values.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/analytics/central_http.go: copy e.AgentID into AggregatedEvent.AgentID.
2. internal/analytics/fleet_sqlite.go migrate: add limit_rule and create user_usage_daily.
3. internal/analytics/fleet_sqlite.go StoreAggregatedEvent: wrap the insert and the rollup upsert in one transaction, upserting only when the insert affected a row.
4. internal/analytics/fleet_sqlite.go prune: add the 35-day rollup prune.
5. internal/analytics: add UserUsage, UserRuleCost and the two query methods on FleetSQLiteStore and CentralStore.
6. Tests: dedup on a retried batch, pruning events keeps rollup totals, migration from an old fleet DB, and SyncWorker to IngestHandler to FleetSQLiteStore carrying agent_id.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] An event synced from a worker with AgentID `claude-code` is returned by GetAggregatedEvents with AgentID `claude-code`: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestIngest_CarriesAgentID`.
- [ ] Ingesting the same batch twice leaves user_usage_daily requests and cost_usd unchanged: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestUserUsageDaily_Dedup`.
- [ ] After pruning every event row by maxEvents, UsageByUser still returns the same totals.
- [ ] An old fleet DB opens with no data loss and a second open is a no-op: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestFleetMigrate_LimitRule`.

### 8/10 · W-P3-PUL-08

**Publish fleet cost blocks as costBlockedUsers from the control plane**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#292](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/292)

A per-worker ledger alone lets a user spend the cap once on every worker. The CP recomputes today's spend per (sub, rule) from the W-P3-PUL-07 rollup and serves over-cap users as costBlockedUsers on the policy wire, appending a publish_log row on every change so signed bundles move to a new seq instead of reading as equivocation. CP only; it runs only when the served policy has a dailyCostUSD rule.

**Requirements**

- A new userCostAggregator in internal/controlplane runs after ingest through the existing `ingest.SetOnEvents` hook, debounced to at most once per 30s, plus once at startup and at each UTC midnight. It runs only when some rule sets DailyCostUSD and the analytics provider is sqlite; with provider memory it logs one WARN and stays off.
- Each run reads `TodayCostByRule` for the current UTC day, looks up each rule's DailyCostUSD by name in the served policy (unknown or removed names are skipped), and builds a sorted `[]config.CostBlockedUser{Sub, Rule, Day}` capped at MaxCostBlockedUsers and checked with ValidateCostBlockedUsers. Anonymous spend is never published.
- The list is computed state merged into policyWire in loadPolicy like blockedUsers and never stored in policy_versions, so a rollback cannot clear it. Entries for past days are never served.
- When the list changes, append a policy_publish_log row with reason `user_cost` (W-P1-PVER-05 pattern) and call policyServer.Refresh so W-P2-SBND-02 bundles get a higher seq and long-poll waiters wake. An unchanged list writes nothing.
- A query error keeps the previous list and ETag, logs one ERROR `user_cost_recompute_failed` without subs, and increments the in-memory `warden_cp_cost_recompute_errors_total`; gauge `warden_cp_cost_blocked_users` holds the list size, both for W-P5-RETN-06 to export.
- With no dailyCostUSD rule, nothing runs and /policy is byte-identical. Logs carry counts only, never emails.
- Capability check: a policy save (dashboard policy write, `warden policy import`, rollback, or an approvals draft when it is applied) that adds a rule with dailyCostUSD or sets dailyCostUSD on an existing rule returns 409 `{"error":"workers_lack_capability","capability":"usercost/v1","workers":[ids]}` while any connected worker lacks `usercost/v1` in its heartbeat caps. `force=true` overrides; only admins may force, and the admin audit row records force and the listed worker ids.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/controlplane/usercost.go (new): userCostAggregator with debounce, midnight timer and last-good list.
2. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: wire it to ingest.SetOnEvents and start it when the conditions hold.
3. internal/controlplane policy server loadPolicy: merge the current list into policyWire.CostBlockedUsers.
4. internal/controlplane: on change, append the `user_cost` publish_log row and call Refresh.
5. Tests with two simulated workers, a fake clock and a failing store fake.
6. internal/controlplane publish path: add the usercost/v1 capability check using the caps stored by W-P1-BLOCK-04, with the force override and its audit details.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Events from worker A ($0.006) and worker B ($0.006) for alice on rule eng-llm with dailyCostUSD 0.01 put `{sub: alice, rule: eng-llm, day: <today>}` in /policy after one run: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestUserCostAggregator`.
- [ ] A change appends one publish_log row with reason `user_cost` and changes the ETag; an unchanged list on the next run changes neither; with `--bundles=offer` the bundle seq increases.
- [ ] With a fake clock past 00:00 UTC the next run serves an empty list.
- [ ] A store error keeps the previous list and ETag.
- [ ] After a CP restart the list is rebuilt from the rollup before the first long-poll is answered.
- [ ] With no dailyCostUSD rule, the /policy body equals the golden: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyWire_UserLimitsAbsentUnchanged`.
- [ ] With one connected worker lacking usercost/v1, saving a rule with dailyCostUSD 5 returns 409 naming that worker and leaves head unchanged; an admin save with force=true succeeds and writes an audit row with force and the worker id; a rateLimit-only rule saves without the check: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestCostCapCapabilityGate`

### 9/10 · W-P3-PUL-09

**Enforce per-user rate limits per request in the proxy**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#293](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/293)

Wire the evaluator's user limits into the worker. Policy and rate limits are checked only at CONNECT today, so a per-user limit would count tunnels, and one keep-alive session can carry requests from several users. Charge each request, h2 stream and WebSocket upgrade in a new userLimitStage, answer 429 with Retry-After, advertise the capability in the heartbeat and lift the PUL-01 guard for rateLimit.

**Requirements**

- `proxy.PolicyEvaluator` gains ChargeUserLimit, PeekUserLimit, MatchUserLimit and IsCostBlocked.
- New `userLimitStage` in runRequestStages after identityStage, blockStage and scopedPolicyStage and before judgeGate, using the request's subject and the worker's resolved agent id. A TLS-terminated CONNECT uses PeekUserLimit only; a raw tunnel without CA is charged once at CONNECT; serveGRPCStream charges per stream; ws.go charges per upgrade.
- Over the limit: 429 with integer Retry-After and JSON `{"error":"user_rate_limited"}`, on the request or the h2 stream; the judge is never called; the deny event goes through p.recordEvent with Reason and LimitRule; RecordBlocked("user_rate_limited") and `warden.user_limit.denied.total{kind=rate}` are recorded.
- Add `user_rate_limited` to internal/proxy/reasons.go and the warden.decision.v1 reason enum with a schema_rev bump. decisionLog gains limit_rule.
- Gauge `warden.user_limit.buckets`; no metric carries a sub, email or group label.
- RemoteProvider.Heartbeat adds `userlimits/v1` to caps. internal/config lifts the guard for rules without dailyCostUSD.
- With no user limits, request handling, events and metrics are unchanged.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/proxy/proxy.go: extend the PolicyEvaluator seam.
2. internal/proxy/http.go: add userLimitStage to runRequestStages and a denyUserRateLimited helper writing the 429.
3. internal/proxy/serve.go handleConn: PeekUserLimit for TLS sessions, ChargeUserLimit for raw tunnels.
4. internal/proxy/grpc.go serveGRPCStream and internal/proxy/ws.go: charge per stream and per upgrade.
5. internal/proxy/reasons.go and docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json: add the reason; internal/observability: add the counter and gauge.
6. internal/worker RemoteProvider heartbeat: add the cap; internal/config: lift the guard for rateLimit-only rules.
7. Tests in internal/proxy using the W-P1-VRFY-01 fake verifier.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Two users on one keep-alive tunnel: only the user over the limit gets 429 with a Retry-After header, and the judge fake gets zero calls: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestUserLimit_RequestStage`.
- [ ] An h2 stream over the limit gets 429 on that stream while other streams continue.
- [ ] A raw tunnel without CA is charged once per CONNECT.
- [ ] Dropping the token puts requests in the anonymous bucket and they are limited by anonymousLimit.
- [ ] The deny event carries user_sub, reason user_rate_limited and limit_rule, and no metric label contains a sub or email.
- [ ] With no user limits configured, `go test ./internal/proxy` passes unchanged.

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-PUL-02`](per-user-limits.md#210--w-p3-pul-02) Record agent id and limit rule on worker events; [`W-P3-PUL-03`](per-user-limits.md#310--w-p3-pul-03) Add per-user limit matching and counters to the policy evaluator; [`W-P1-GPOL-03`](identity-policy.md#39--w-p1-gpol-03) Apply group-aware allow decisions at CONNECT and request time; [`W-P1-BLOCK-02`](user-block-list.md#29--w-p1-block-02) Enforce the block list in the worker at CONNECT, per request and per h2 stream; [`W-P1-JAUD-06`](audit-log-export.md#26--w-p1-jaud-06) Set a bounded Reason on every deny event; [`W-P1-JAUD-02`](audit-log-export.md#46--w-p1-jaud-02) Publish decision v1 JSON Schema with closed-field and leak tests

### 10/10 · W-P3-PUL-10

**Add per-user limits end-to-end test and docs**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue [#294](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/294)

Prove the done-when end to end with two workers and one CP under the integration build tag, and document how per-user limits behave, including where they are approximate. Operators need the overshoot bounds, the anonymous and raw-tunnel rules and the UTC-day reset written down before relying on caps.

**Requirements**

- An integration test under `//go:build integration` with two in-process CA-enabled workers, one CP with the sqlite fleet store and the in-process OIDC issuer from W-P1-VRFY-05.
- It covers a rate deny for one user while another continues, survival of the window across an unrelated policy change, a cost cap on one worker with streamed responses, the CP-published costBlockedUsers stopping the user on the second worker, the anonymous bucket, and the usage endpoint totals.
